text: Replace existing consumer unit (fuse board)
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: NICEIC states that installing or replacing a consumer unit is notifiable Part P work in England and Wales, to be done by a scheme-registered installer or approved by building control.

text: Install a new radial circuit for kitchen sockets
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: Planning Portal lists installing a complete new circuit (e.g. ring or lighting circuit) as notifiable electrical work in England.

text: Install an electric shower on a new circuit from the consumer unit
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: Planning Portal gives a new circuit for a shower as an example of notifiable work.

text: Install a new dedicated cooker circuit for a built-in oven
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: AD P para 2.8 says a built-in cooker becomes notifiable when a new cooker circuit is needed.

text: Fit a built-in oven to the existing cooker circuit (no new circuit)
label: not_notifiable
source_claim: AD P para 2.8 says installing a built-in cooker is not notifiable unless a new cooker circuit is required.

text: Install an EV charge point on a new dedicated circuit
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: Planning Portal says a home EV charger is notifiable because it creates a new circuit, unless done by a competent person scheme installer who certifies it.

text: Connect an electric gate motor to an existing isolator switch
label: not_notifiable
source_claim: AD P para 2.8 says connecting an electric gate or garage door to an existing isolator is not notifiable.

text: Run a new circuit from the consumer unit to an isolator for an electric garage door
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: AD P para 2.8 says running a new circuit from the consumer unit to the isolator is notifiable.

text: Add extra socket outlets to the existing kitchen ring circuit
label: not_notifiable
source_claim: Planning Portal says additions to existing circuits outside special locations are not notifiable, and that in England special locations are only the spaces around baths and showers (kitchens are special only in Wales).

text: Add a fused spur from an existing ring circuit in a living room
label: not_notifiable
source_claim: ECA's Part P FAQ says a new spur from an existing circuit can be added without scheme registration if not in a special location.

text: Add fixed garden lighting fed from an existing circuit
label: not_notifiable
source_claim: Electrical Safety First says the April 2013 Part P changes removed notification requirements for areas such as kitchens and outdoors; AD P 2.2 keeps garden lighting within Part P scope but 2.7 makes additions outside special locations non-notifiable.

text: Install a new circuit from the house to a detached garden shed
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: NICEIC states that a new circuit from the house to an outdoor building is notifiable Part P work in England and Wales.

text: Replace an existing ceiling light fitting like-for-like
label: not_notifiable
source_claim: AD P para 2.7 says replacements, repairs and maintenance anywhere are not notifiable.

text: Add a new light fitting directly above the bath
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: NICEIC says any installation or alteration within bathroom zones 0, 1 or 2 (e.g. lights above a bath) is notifiable.

text: Add a light point in a bathroom more than 0.6 m horizontally from the bath edge (outside the special location)
label: not_notifiable
source_claim: AD P defines the bathroom special location as the space within 0.6 m of the bath/shower tray up to 2.25 m, and 2.7 says additions outside special locations are not notifiable.

text: Add a socket outlet in a room containing a sauna heater
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: AD P para 2.5 (quoting reg 12(9)) treats a whole room containing a swimming pool or sauna heater as a special location, so additions there are notifiable.

text: Full electrical rewire of a house
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: NICEIC lists a full rewire, new circuits and consumer unit changes as notifiable work needing a Part P compliance certificate.

text: Replace a gas combi boiler with a new condensing boiler
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: Planning Portal says installing a new boiler needs Building Regulations approval and the gas installer should be Gas Safe registered.

text: Install a new gas fire
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: Gas Safe's factsheet lists installing gas appliances such as boilers and gas fires as building work that its registered businesses must notify to the local authority.

text: Install an unvented hot water cylinder (over 15 litres)
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: LABC says hot water storage over 15 litres must be notified by building notice, full plans, or a competent person scheme installer.

text: Install a point-of-use water heater of 15 litres or less on an existing circuit
label: not_notifiable
source_claim: LABC says units storing 15 litres or less, with exempt electrical supply, need not be notified though still must comply.

text: Replace an oil-fired boiler
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: OFTEC says new heating equipment such as boilers must be notified to building control in England, and OFTEC-registered installers can self-certify.

text: Install a new domestic oil storage tank
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: OFTEC says fuel storage tanks are heating equipment that must be notified, with self-certification available via OFTEC registration.

text: Install a wood-burning stove into an existing chimney
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: HETAS says every solid fuel installation in England must be notified to building control, either via a scheme like HETAS or directly by the householder before work starts.

text: Build a new masonry chimney for a wood-burning stove
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
source_claim: Schedule 3 paras 1-3 (gas, oil, solid fuel appliances) each state they do not apply to providing a masonry chimney, so it cannot be self-certified.

text: Install a new wet central heating system
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: GOV.UK lists installing or replacing a heating system among work needing building regulations approval; Schedule 3 para 4 allows competent person self-certification.

text: Fit thermostatic radiator valves to existing radiators
label: not_notifiable
source_claim: Schedule 4 para 1(f) exempts adding a control device to an existing fixed building service where testing and adjustment is not possible or would not affect energy use.

text: Install an air source heat pump
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: Planning Portal says building regulations normally apply to an air source heat pump and advises an MCS or competent person scheme installer.

text: Install roof-mounted solar PV panels
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: Planning Portal says building regulations apply to roof solar panels (roof load check and electrical work) and recommends a competent person scheme installer.

text: Replace existing uPVC windows with new double-glazed units in same openings
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: Replacement windows are controlled fittings; a registered competent person scheme installer can certify them, otherwise apply to a building control body.

text: Replace front door with new door more than half glazed (door and frame)
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: Regulations apply to a new door only when over 50% of door and frame is glazed; a registered competent person can self-certify, otherwise make an application.

text: Replace external back door with solid door, glazing under 50% of door and frame
label: not_notifiable
source_claim: GOV.UK lists external doors with less than half the door glazed among work not needing building regulations approval.

text: Widen existing window opening and fit new lintel and larger window
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
source_claim: For new or widened openings an application is needed for the structural opening and lintel even if a competent person fits the window.

text: Install new rooflight in existing pitched roof (cut rafters, trimmers)
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
source_claim: Approval is generally needed for a new rooflight because the roof structure must be altered to form the opening and carry the load.

text: Replace existing rooflight with new unit in same opening
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: Schedule 3 para 10 lets a registered person self-certify replacement windows, rooflights, roof windows or doors in an existing dwelling.

text: Strip and re-cover whole pitched roof with like-for-like tiles
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: Replacement of roof coverings on pitched and flat roofs is self-certifiable work under NAPIT or CompetentRoofer schemes.

text: Repair small area of roof covering (under 25% of roof, like-for-like)
label: not_notifiable
source_claim: Repairs or re-covering affecting under 25% of the envelope and under 50% of the roof normally need no building control application.

text: Inject cavity wall insulation into existing masonry cavity walls
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: Cavity wall insulation is specifically notifiable; a building notice is required unless a registered installer handles notification.

text: Install external wall insulation and render system to solid walls
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: Schedule 3 para 19 lists installing insulation to external walls as work a registered person can self-certify.

text: Dry-line inside of external solid walls with insulated plasterboard
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: Schedule 3 para 18 lists installing insulation to internal walls (excluding flexible thermal linings) as self-certifiable by registered persons.

text: Lay mineral wool loft insulation between and over ceiling joists (insulation only)
label: not_notifiable
source_claim: GOV.UK says installing insulation in roof spaces does not need building regulations approval.

text: Insulate under suspended timber ground floor (insulation only, no floor replacement)
label: not_notifiable
source_claim: GOV.UK says installing insulation under timber floors does not need building regulations approval.

text: Remove and re-render more than 25% of external wall area
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
source_claim: Re-rendering 25% or more counts as renovation of a thermal element needing insulation and a building regulations application.

text: Replace rainwater gutters and downpipes
label: not_notifiable
source_claim: GOV.UK lists gutters or downpipes among work not needing building regulations approval.

text: Replace bath, WC and basin like-for-like in same positions
label: not_notifiable
source_claim: Like-for-like replacement of bathroom units and fittings does not normally need building control approval.

text: Form new en-suite shower room in bedroom connecting to existing soil stack
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: A completely new en-suite needs approval; a competent person can self-certify it, otherwise an application is needed.

text: Install whole-house mechanical ventilation with heat recovery (MVHR)
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: Schedule 3 para 6 lets registered persons self-certify a ventilation or air conditioning system in a dwelling not shared with others.

text: Relocate WC and basin with new connection to underground drain
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
source_claim: Relocating bathroom fittings with new connections to a stack or underground drain is controllable work needing approval.

text: Remove loadbearing internal wall and install steel beam on padstones
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
source_claim: All structural alterations, including knocking down load-bearing walls, require building regulations approval.

text: Remove non-loadbearing stud wall between lounge and entrance hall/stairs
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
source_claim: Taking out a non-loadbearing wall that separates a room from the hall, stair or landing needs a building regulations application.

text: Underpin part of house foundations after subsidence
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
source_claim: Underpinning is defined as building work and normally requires building regulations approval with a structural design.

text: Convert loft into habitable bedroom with new stair
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
source_claim: Converting a loft into liveable space requires building regulations approval covering structure, fire escape and stairs.

text: Convert integral garage into habitable room
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
source_claim: Converting all or part of a garage into habitable space normally requires building regulations approval.

text: Build 20 m2 ground-level conservatory separated by external doors, independent heating
label: not_notifiable
source_claim: Ground-level conservatories under 30 m2, separated by external-quality doors with independent heating, are normally exempt.

text: Remove external doors between house and existing conservatory to open plan
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
source_claim: Removing exterior doors or walls between the house and a conservatory needs building regulations approval as the exemption is lost.

text: Build 20 m2 garden room with bedroom for guests
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
source_claim: Small detached buildings escape the regulations only if they contain no sleeping accommodation.

text: Inject chemical damp-proof course into existing walls
label: not_notifiable
source_claim: Installing or replacing a damp-proof course in most instances does not require building regulations approval.

text: Internal redecoration: wallpaper, paint and new skirting boards
label: not_notifiable
source_claim: Internal decorating such as wallpapering, painting or new skirting boards does not normally require approval.

text: Replace kitchen units and worktops in same layout
label: not_notifiable
source_claim: Refitting a kitchen with new units and fittings does not generally require approval, though drainage or electrics may.

text: New office building
label: full_plans_required
source_claim: Brent lists buildings covered by the Fire Safety Order, including offices, shops, factories and workplaces, as needing a full plans application rather than a building notice.

text: Internal alterations to an office that change the means of escape
label: full_plans_required
source_claim: Stratford says a building notice cannot be used for non-domestic work affecting means of escape or for non-domestic buildings subject to the Fire Safety Order.

text: Structural alterations during a shop fit-out
label: full_plans_required
source_claim: Oxford states a building notice cannot be used for commercial works or premises covered by the Fire Safety Order such as shops, factories and offices.

text: Extension to a factory
label: full_plans_required
source_claim: East Staffordshire says building notices cannot be used for offices, shops, hotels, boarding houses or certain factories, so full plans are needed.

text: Alterations to a hotel
label: full_plans_required
source_claim: East Staffordshire lists hotels and boarding houses among building uses for which a building notice cannot be used.

text: Alterations to a bed and breakfast guesthouse
label: full_plans_required
source_claim: GOV.UK says fire safety law covers workplaces, premises open to the public and paying-guest accommodation such as B&Bs; with reg 12(3) this means full plans.

text: Alterations to a public building such as a community hall
label: full_plans_required
source_claim: Oxford lists public buildings among Fire Safety Order premises where a building notice cannot be used.

text: New fire doors and partitions in the common stairwell of a block of flats
label: full_plans_required
source_claim: Preston says full plans must always be used for works in the common parts of buildings containing flats and houses in multiple occupation.

text: Alterations to a house in multiple occupation
label: full_plans_required
source_claim: Brent requires full plans for residential properties with shared areas, naming flats, maisonettes, hotels and houses in multiple occupation.

text: Work to a converted building containing flats with shared common areas
label: full_plans_required
source_claim: Swindon says a building notice cannot be used for flats with common areas or for work to non-domestic buildings.

text: Converting a house into self-contained flats with a shared entrance
context: House being converted to flats in England
label: full_plans_required
source_claim: Planning Portal says full plans are always needed where the Fire Safety Order applies or will apply after the work is completed.

text: Change of use of a house to a shop
label: full_plans_required
source_claim: Planning Portal says full plans are required where the Fire Safety Order will apply to the building once the work is complete.

text: Work to a workplace or premises where the Fire Safety Order applies
label: full_plans_required
source_claim: The partnership says full plans are required where the Fire Safety Order applies, which covers almost all buildings other than private houses and flat interiors.

text: New house fronting onto a private street
label: full_plans_required
source_claim: Dover says the building notice route cannot be used for a new building fronting a private street and full plans are needed instead.

text: New building facing a private road
label: full_plans_required
source_claim: Brent lists a building facing a private road among cases needing a full plans application.

text: New dwellings on an unadopted estate road
label: full_plans_required
source_claim: GOV.UK notes many new dwellings front a private street at application stage, so full plans are needed and a building notice would be invalid.

text: New building on a site fronting a private street
label: full_plans_required
source_claim: Hertfordshire Building Control says a full plans application is needed where the property fronts a private road.

text: Rear extension to a house within 3 m of a public sewer
label: full_plans_required
source_claim: Brent requires full plans for extensions built over or within three metres of a public sewer.

text: Extension built directly over a public sewer
label: full_plans_required
source_claim: Swindon says a building notice cannot be used for work to any building above or within 3 metres of a public sewer.

text: Underpinning a house within 3 m of a public sewer
label: full_plans_required
source_claim: East Staffordshire says building notices cannot be used for buildings, extensions or underpinning within 3 metres of a public sewer.

text: New detached building close to a drain shown on the sewer map
label: full_plans_required
source_claim: Planning Portal says full plans are required for work built close to or over drains shown on the map of sewers.

text: House extension within 3 m of a public sewer where a build-over agreement is already in place
label: full_plans_required
source_claim: Regulation 12(5) requires full plans wherever H4 imposes a requirement, with no exception for work that already has a water company build-over agreement.

text: Extension within 3 m of a non-public sewer shown on the sewer records
label: full_plans_required
source_claim: Approved Document H says H4 covers building or extending within 3 m of a drain or sewer on the undertaker's records, public or not.

text: Single-storey rear extension to a house away from sewers and not on a private street
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
source_claim: The Hampshire partnership says building notices are generally used for smaller works such as single-storey extensions, subject to the sewer and private street exclusions.

text: Removing one or two internal walls in a house
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
source_claim: Oxford lists internal alterations removing one or two walls as suitable straightforward domestic work for a building notice.

text: Underpinning house foundations with no sewer nearby
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
source_claim: Sevenoaks says a building notice is only for domestic work and suits smaller jobs such as underpinning, internal alterations or re-roofing.

text: Internal alterations inside a single flat not affecting common parts
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
source_claim: The partnership notes the Fire Safety Order does not apply inside individual flats, only to common areas, so the full plans trigger is not met.

text: Replacement windows in an office fitted by a FENSA-registered installer
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: Schedule 3 paragraph 11 lets registered installers such as FENSA self-certify replacement windows and doors in buildings other than dwellings.

text: Replacement windows in a house fitted by a FENSA-registered installer
label: competent_person_scheme
source_claim: Schedule 3 paragraph 10 lets registered installers such as FENSA self-certify replacement windows and doors in existing dwellings.
